facts.raw_span: born at 35 weeks 4 days’ gestation
weighing 2152 g
one of monochorionic diamniotic twins
her identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
Fetal ultrasound had shown microcephaly and ventricular enlargement
Postnatal MRI of the head revealed microcephaly, marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles without signs of elevated intracranial pressure
severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum were preserved
No intracranial hematoma or neoplastic lesions were seen
very weak light reflexes bilaterally
mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign
No chorioretinal dysplasia was noted

support_spans: one of monochorionic diamniotic twins
her identical twin died in utero at 24 weeks
concepts.why: The presence of monochorionic diamniotic twins and the death of the identical twin in utero support this diagnosis.

support_spans: severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes
the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum were preserved
concepts.why: The severe thinning of the frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes and the preservation of the temporal lobes, basal ganglia, thalamus, brain stem, and cerebellum support this diagnosis.
It explains the weak light reflexes and optic nerve pallor in the context of cerebral dysgenesis and absence of other ocular abnormalities.

rationales.F03: Monochorionic diamniotic twins is a risk factor for complications such as twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome, which can lead to fetal akinesia deformation sequence and cerebral dysgenesis.
rationales.F04: The death of one twin in utero can lead to complications in the surviving twin, including fetal akinesia deformation sequence and cerebral dysgenesis.
rationales.F05: Microcephaly and ventricular enlargement are characteristic features of fetal akinesia deformation sequence and congenital hydrocephalus.
rationales.F06: The presence of microcephaly and marked enlargement of both lateral ventricles without signs of elevated intracranial pressure is consistent with congenital hydrocephalus and cerebral dysgenesis.
rationales.F10: Weak light reflexes can be a sign of optic nerve hypoplasia or Leber congenital amaurosis.
rationales.F11: Mild optic nerve pallor with suspected peripapillary double-ring sign is a characteristic feature of optic nerve hypoplasia.
